_readme: Fix playbook for opcode_inspector.py. Edit freely; the script reloads it on every scan.
Keys are emu opcode names. Inside each, '*' applies to every client; a client name (RoF2, SoD) overrides it.
Never write hex values here. Reference opcodes by name and the script looks the value up in your .conf
map_to: OP_Name        -> suggests <this opcode>=<value of OP_Name> (same packet, different name)
new_opcode: OP_Name    -> suggests adding OP_Name=<upstream value> (new emu opcode needed)
same_layout: [ours, upstream] -> struct names checked against each other when upstream data is loaded
expect_upstream_unmapped: true -> the advice assumes upstream has no value; flagged if that changes
requires_encoder: OP_Name -> the advice relies on your patch encoding OP_Name; flagged if it doesn't
In text: {client}, {map_to}, {map_value}, {value:OP_Name} are filled in at scan time.
action is one of: MAP, REROUTE, SERVER, PORT, NOT NEEDED, CUSTOM, INVESTIGATE.

RoF2.summary: {client} calls this {map_to} ({map_value}). Your GuildManageRemove_Struct {{uint32 guild_id; char name[64]}} has the same layout as upstream's GuildMemberDelete_Struct, so mapping the opcode is enough.
Rank changes. {client} uses OP_SetGuildRank ({value:OP_SetGuildRank}; upstream calls it OP_GuildMemberRankAltBanker), which your {client} patch already encodes. Translate GuildManageStatus into it.
Member joined. {client} uses OP_GuildMemberAdd ({value:OP_GuildMemberAdd}); upstream sends it with GuildMemberAdd_Struct. Needs a new emu opcode, a .conf line, a wire struct and an encoder.

*.summary: Upstream removed this packet entirely. {client} gets the guild list from OP_GuildsList, which your {client} patch already encodes. For {client} clients send (or rely on) OP_GuildsList instead; check what the sender in guild.cpp is for before removing it.
No {client} opcode (upstream sends it unmapped, so {client} players never see these messages). Deliver it as ordinary chat for {client}.

Upstream no longer has this packet. {client} shows item details via OP_ItemLinkResponse (encoded by your patch). Check what the senders in client.cpp deliver and route it through OP_ItemLinkResponse or a chat message with an item link.
No {client} opcode; upstream sends it unmapped too. Other players see the LFG flag from spawn data (the lfg field in OP_ZoneSpawns/OP_NewSpawn), not from this packet.
{client} finishes zone-in without it; upstream sends it unmapped on every zone-in.
No {client} opcode; upstream sends it unmapped. Camp/logout runs on OP_Camp and OP_Logout.
No {client} opcode; upstream sends it unmapped. The player still gets the 'You cannot see your target' message.
No {client} opcode; upstream sends it unmapped. The trainer window closes client-side.
{client} has no petition window opcodes (all 0 upstream). GMs use #petition commands.
{client} has no petition window opcodes (all 0 upstream). GMs use #petition commands.
Part of the old bazaar protocol. Upstream rewrote the bazaar around OP_TraderShop, OP_BazaarSearch and OP_Trader actions; {client} trader updates only work after porting that.
Old bazaar protocol; no {client} opcode. See upstream's bazaar rewrite (OP_TraderShop / OP_BazaarSearch).
{client} doesn't send OP_TraderBuy; purchases arrive as OP_TraderShop actions in upstream's bazaar. Your D(OP_TraderBuy) can never run for {client}.

RoF2.summary: Handle_OP_Camp already uses the server-side camp_timer for {client}; this packet is for your modified SoD client.

SoD.summary: Only your modified SoD client knows this opcode. Add OP_ResetCampTimer=<value from that client> to patch_SoD.conf.

*.summary: Private anti-cheat diagnostics (PRODUCTION builds, libsoddiag). Only a modified client sends it; it has no opcode in either .conf, so it never arrives. Leave it unless that client is in use.
Placeholder name with no value in any .conf. Find what the sender in client_packet.cpp was meant to do; delete the send if it's leftover.

RoF2.summary: {client} calls it {map_to} ({map_value}). Your patch_SoD.conf already maps both names to one value.
